---
title: "Follow a Calculation Through the Code"
subtitle: "Find the inputs, equations, and result behind a serving scenario."
---

A named scenario connects an input configuration to a calculation. To understand
its result, follow that connection through the implementation. The same route
helps a contributor find the file that owns a proposed change.

## Start from the public call

The named serving case below selects a workload, a device, a context length, and
a batch size. Its `result` property invokes the serving model.

```{python}
from mlsysim import Scenarios

case = Scenarios.Llama3_70B_ServingH100
result = case.result
print("Scenario type:", type(case).__name__)
print("Result type:", type(result).__name__)
print("Fits modeled memory:", result.feasible)
```

Feasibility is part of the result. A latency estimate alone does not establish
that the selected workload fits the device. For an introduction to the public
interfaces and their different scopes, see [Choosing a Python API](choosing-an-api.qmd).

## Find the owner of each part

The serving domain uses the same name across scenario definitions, named
configurations, and result schemas. These files have different responsibilities.

| Part | File under `mlsysim/engine/` | What to read |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Named inputs | `scenario_catalog/serving/foundations.py` | `Llama3_70B_ServingH100`: the selected workload, hardware, and scenario assumptions |
| Typed scenario | `scenario_definitions/serving.py` | `ServingScenario`: its input fields and `result` property |
| Solver | `solvers/serving.py` | `ServingModel.solve`: the parameters, accounting, validity regime, and exclusions |
| Result | `result_types/serving.py` | `ServingResult`: returned fields, units, and feasibility semantics |

`ServingScenario.result` passes the configured inputs to `ServingModel.solve`.
The solver combines reusable equations and shared serving accounting. Its imports
point to the specific owners: transformer work in `physics/transformer.py`, KV
storage in `physics/memory.py`, and the shared decode calculation in
`engine/solvers/_decode.py`. Read the solver's docstring before interpreting a
helper in isolation; it states which costs the composed estimate includes.

The [serving scenario reference](api/scenario-domain-serving.qmd) links related
contracts. Each class page identifies the file that defines it. The
[domain directory](api/scenario-domains.qmd) follows the same organization for
training, communication, data, and the other modeling subjects.

## Keep public imports stable

Textbooks and applications continue to import `Scenarios`, `mlsysim.solvers`,
and the established scenario and result classes. The modules
`engine/scenario_types.py`, `engine/scenarios.py`, and `engine/results.py`
forward those imports to the domain implementations. They provide compatibility;
a calculation has one implementation in its defining module.

Historical class metadata is preserved for serialization compatibility. It may
therefore identify the older public module rather than the file that now owns
the class. Use the source locations in the generated reference when navigating
the implementation.

A domain describes a modeling subject, not a textbook volume. A serving scenario
can support several volumes, a lab, and a paper without moving or acquiring a
second implementation.

## Make a change reviewable

First identify whether the proposal changes a specification, a scenario input,
an equation, or a result's presentation. Edit its owner. A hardware specification
belongs with its sourced registry data; a different context length belongs in a
scenario configuration; a different accounting assumption belongs with the
calculation and its documented contract.

For serving behavior, start with `tests/test_physical_contracts.py`,
`tests/test_shared_accounting.py`, and `tests/test_solver_suite.py`.
`tests/test_calculation_scenarios.py` exercises named cases. The test directory's
`README.md` maps these checks to the broader suite. Documentation examples check
that the stated calls run; physical contracts check the calculation's units,
accounting, and limiting behavior.

A source move should preserve those behaviors. A numerical correction needs a
separate explanation of the changed assumption and its downstream consequences.
Run the [modeling documentation checks](modeling-conventions.qmd), then compare
the affected textbook and paper consumers using the release runbook's downstream
snapshot workflow. Surface changed prose claims for editorial review rather than
silently updating their numbers.
